clue.text: She takes it to be an eye infection

indicators.note: takes means the woman's name holds the next word inside it

parts.note: Iris is a girl's name, so 'she' can stand for her
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman accepts that she has an infection of the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' stands for a woman's name; the eye link in the surface is apt, since that name is also part of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the coloured ring around the pupil is a medical condition of the eye.

clue.text: Odd policeman takes a rest day?

explanation.surface: A strange police officer decides to take a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: A constable's regular patrol round is his beat; on a rest day he is literally off it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconventional or quirky behaviour is called odd; and a constable not walking his patrol round is away from it.

clue.text: Made moral play into emotional drama

indicators.note: play suggests the letters are toyed with and moved freely into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone turned a moral tale into a tearjerker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a noun for the stage, but it is the signal to rearrange MADE MORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensational, overwrought stage piece or situation is the classic example of exaggerated feeling.

clue.text: There's a stripe on the bag containing wine

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: a bar is a stripe, as on a uniform or flag
a sac is a bag or pouch, especially in biology

explanation.surface: A striped bag has a bottle of wine inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet white dessert wine from the Bordeaux region of France.

clue.text: It's awkward left handed

explanation.surface: Someone who is left-handed is clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word for left also means socially clumsy in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Socially clumsy or tactless is one sense; the French source word means on the left side.

clue.text: Weapon material which is grey

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
metal is a material, such as iron or steel

explanation.surface: The stuff a weapon is made of is grey.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark bluish-grey colour, named after the bronze alloy once used for cannon.

clue.text: An initial point could have been brighter

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'An initial point could have been brighter': no parse of these words builds UNLIT (UNIT round L would need a word for L); likely garbled in OCR and no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: An initial point could have been brighter

clue.text: People not well treated here

parts.note: reads like a complaint about poor service, but means those who are sick receive care in this place

explanation.surface: A complaint about a place where customers are badly looked after.
explanation.definitionFit: An institution where the sick and injured receive medical care.

clue.text: Sack a fellow soldier

parts.note: to sack a place is to plunder or ransack it, also rifle
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: Someone advises firing a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' suggests dismissal, but here it means plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: An infantry soldier armed with a long gun is the classic example of a private in arms.

clue.text: Confine in quarters which are nearby

parts.note: east and north are two of the four quarters of the compass
close means nearby

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep someone shut in rooms close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like lodgings, but stands for two compass points, E and N.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut in or surround on all sides is to restrict something within limits.

clue.text: Expressions of thanks and disapproval are banned!

parts.note: ta is an informal British word for thanks
boo is a jeer expressing disapproval

explanation.surface: Saying thank you and booing are both forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden by custom or rule is off limits, prohibited.

clue.text: Taking arsenic?-sure to find out

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
certain means sure

explanation.surface: Someone is sure that dosing with poison will reveal the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine or establish a fact is to discover it by checking.

clue.text: Retiring money lender lost his hair

indicators.note: lost means a piece is dropped from the moneylender's name

parts.note: Shylock is the moneylender in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice
a lock is a tuft of hair

explanation.surface: A moneylender who is retiring has gone bald.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' suggests leaving work, but here it means bashful; take LOCK (hair) from SHYLOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A timid, bashful person tends to withdraw from company.

clue.text: One of three in a fire which was ineffective

definitions.text: One of three in a fire which was ineffective

parts.words: One of three in a fire which was ineffective
parts.note: refers to the Book of Daniel, where three young men thrown into a fiery furnace emerged unburnt

explanation.surface: One of three people caught in a blaze that did no harm.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible, Nebuchadnezzar threw three Hebrews into a furnace; the flames did not touch them.
explanation.definitionFit: He is one of the trio of young Jews, with Meshach and Abednego, saved from Nebuchadnezzar's furnace.

clue.text: Be seen to distribute a paper

indicators.note: distribute means spread the letters around into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper wants to be noticed by handing out copies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribute' looks like delivering a newspaper but signals rearranging A PAPER.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into view or become visible is to show up.

clue.text: Hackneyed remark from a quiet position

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
latitude gives a position north or south of the equator

explanation.surface: A tired cliche spoken from a calm stance.
explanation.definitionFit: A trite, overused saying is a stale commonplace.

clue.text: Half a dozen had a whip round and produced an overgenerous response

indicators.note: round means the whipping word goes around the number

parts.note: lashed means struck with a whip
half a dozen is six, VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Six people chipped in and responded far too generously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had a whip round' suggests passing the hat for a collection, but the whipping word goes round the number.
explanation.definitionFit: To give or bestow in excessive quantity is to heap upon someone extravagantly.

clue.text: It might take a month

explanation.surface: Something could take thirty days.
explanation.definitionFit: A modal verb expressing possibility; and the fifth calendar entry of the year, between April and June.

clue.text: Tune plus verse for high fliers

parts.note: an air is a tune
lines of verse make a poem

explanation.surface: Music and poetry for ambitious people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high fliers' suggests ambitious people, but means companies that fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Companies operating scheduled passenger flights carry people through the sky.

clue.text: One with a fifty fifty chance of a cure perhaps

definitions.text: One with a fifty fifty chance of a cure perhaps

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a second L for the second fifty

explanation.surface: A patient whose odds of recovery are even.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifty fifty' suggests even odds, but gives two Roman fifties.
explanation.definitionFit: A sick person is someone who may hope to be cured.

clue.text: Found between Zechariah and Zephaniah

parts.note: the Old Testament minor prophets run Zephaniah, then this book, then Zechariah

explanation.surface: Something located between two Old Testament prophets.
explanation.definitionFit: A short book of the Old Testament placed after Zephaniah and before Zechariah.

clue.text: Carpet acquired using inside information

indicators.note: inside means the letters sit within the last word

explanation.surface: Floor covering obtained with insider knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside information' sounds like a tip-off, but signals letters inside 'information'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rug or floor covering laid down on a floor.

clue.text: Town in Cyprus with a canal right round

indicators.note: round suggests turning the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A Cypriot town circled by a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like the canal encircling the town but signals rearranging A CANAL plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: A port city on the southern coast of Cyprus with the island's main airport.

clue.text: Sailor's piece of land was a figment of his imagination

parts.note: AB (able seaman) is a sailor, with the possessive S
a tract is an expanse of land

explanation.surface: A sailor's plot of land turned out to be imaginary.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea existing only in thought, not as a concrete thing, is notional.

clue.text: Way round found by father on the ship

parts.note: taken as written
pa is an informal word for father
SS (steamship) is a ship

explanation.surface: Dad discovers a route around while aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A road built to divert traffic around a town is a diversion route.

clue.text: Some variety of hornet was found on the seat

indicators.note: variety of suggests a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of wasp is spotted sitting on a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of hornet' looks like a species of wasp, but signals rearranging HORNET.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's ceremonial chair is a seat of state.

clue.text: Meeting obligations on the outskirts of Llanelli takes great skill!

definitions.note: plural in the clue against a singular answer, which as a mass noun means legal responsibility

indicators.note: outskirts means taking only the first and last letters of the town's name

parts.note: ability is great skill or talent

explanation.surface: Fulfilling duties on the edge of a Welsh town demands real talent.
explanation.walkthrough: LLANELLI is a town in South Wales; its first and last letters give LI.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal responsibility for debts or duties is a burden owed.

clue.text: Being drunk on this!

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: This is what makes a person intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' signals rearranging BEING; the whole clue also describes a drinking session.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout of heavy drinking is the occasion of getting intoxicated.

clue.text: Singer submitted sick note at the end of December

indicators.note: sick suggests the letters are unwell and so muddled into a new order
at the end of picks the last letter of the month

explanation.surface: A vocalist handed in a doctor's note late in December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick note' looks like a medical certificate, but 'sick' rearranges NOTE to TENO; then R closes December.
explanation.definitionFit: A male voice range above baritone is that of a high male vocalist.

clue.text: Calling on the quiet and getting sharper

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
honing means sharpening

explanation.surface: Ringing someone secretly while sharpening a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the quiet' suggests secrecy, but means P comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringing someone on the telephone is making a call.

clue.text: I soon managed to include the retired policeman in a piece of sacred music

indicators.note: to include means the rearranged letters hold the next part inside
retired means the police word is drawn back, read in reverse

parts.note: the CID (Criminal Investigation Department) is the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: Someone retired from the force quickly arranges a hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' is only a link here: the letters of I SOON stay in order, and the turned-back police abbreviation sits inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A short hymn or chant in the Eastern Orthodox liturgy is a devotional composition.

clue.text: They're cold & calculating!

explanation.surface: Some people are heartless and scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: Snakes are cold-blooded; calculating machines add up.
explanation.definitionFit: Venomous snakes are cold-blooded creatures; and machines that sum figures are calculators.
